scenes.say: A population consists of members of one species in an area. Births and immigration add individuals; deaths and emigration remove them. Crowding can intensify competition for food or help disease spread. Effects that vary with density are density-dependent.
A quadrat marks a known area. Counts from several samples can estimate how many plants or slow animals live per unit area.

Winged reproductive termites leave the nest in mating flights. Dispersers can establish new colonies after mating. In a large simultaneous swarm, predators may eat many termites but can only eat so many. Some reproductives escape and disperse.

JAMB asks what population dynamics studies, which effects increase when a population is crowded and why termite reproductives fly out together. The blue arrows show direction of movement or change over time.

quickCheck.prompt: Which tool samples plant abundance in a fixed area?
quickCheck.feedback: A quadrat marks a known area so counts from different places can be compared.
